# 1\. Purpose

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines the guidelines and procedures for the User Value Model Science On-Call rotation. The purpose of this SOP is to ensure efficient and effective response to incidents, proactive monitoring of the user value model, and consistent communication among the team.

# 2\. Scope

This SOP applies to all members of the User Value Model team participating in the on-call rotation.

# 3\. Daily monitoring tasks

**Update 5/7: Blacklist/Blocklist should now follow this [SOP](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ads-event-blocklist/blob/master/usage.md) (if model includes this [commit](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/vector-ai-unity-learner/commit/69152e91ed0fc11c8c940a03ad50c0b153d3893b) \- Apr 24, 2026 / [Quick Link to Studio](https://console.cloud.google.com/sql/instances/ads-blocklist-instance/studio?inv=1&invt=Ab4LCQ&project=unity-ads-cpi-direct-prd))**

* [Useful code for blocking list](https://docs.google.com/document/d/10plHDewMOrOS5c4w4THBWesBljsDoDTFA4MZDl12gSA/edit?usp=sharing): Internal Queries \- use SOP above for blocking steps, etc. \- this doc has additional useful queries for reference.  

Useful dashboards to monitor: 

1. WoW trends for the last week in  ML [Imply dashboard](https://internal-v2-1.pivot.int-prd-imply.unity3d.com/pivot/i/0a6d67afa1f9c72550/uAds_Direct_Demand_ML_\(event_ts_timestamp\)) to monitor immediate change, and use [Demand supply dashboard](https://internal-v2-1.pivot.int-prd-imply.unity3d.com/pivot/i/ea229d7d2491ebdfc8/uAds_Demand_Supply_Internal_\(billing_&_finance\)) (data cube: uAds Demand Supply \- Internal (billing & finance)) to monitor D0 ROAS metrics 2 days later.  
   1. WoW trends can be misleading when the past week included either incidents or holidays (anomalous seasonality). Confirm anomalous trends with Wo2W and Wo3W before triggering a larger investigation.   
2. Look for failures of prod pipelines (tagged with [@ads-user-value-dev](https://unity.enterprise.slack.com/admin/user_groups)s) in [\#ads-app-alerts-prod](https://unity.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C050WP149S8)  
   1. Single failures are common and not cause for concern. Investigations are only needed for cases where the same pipeline fails multiple (\>=2) times in a row.   
   2. Frequence failures interlaced with successes are usually a sign of infra instability and these cases should be escalated to MLEs  
3. Check for data alerts in [\#app-data-alerts](https://unity.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C04ERGC9V9N), only:   
   1. [**Low (\<= 0.2$) Percent of row** reached **0.05** has been triggered](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C04ERGC9V9N/p1756789358494009). When these alerts trigger, DS needs to [blacklist the faulty target id(s)](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ads-audience-pinpointer/blob/main/runbooks/BLACKLIST.md) and alert the @ads-attribution-mmp-data DE on-call to blacklist on their side as well.   
4. Check for feature & label drift   
   1. Check for label drift, using the temporary BQ query in the appendix  
   2. Check for feature drift (with Feature drift \- User Value Looker), focusing on the arrays WoW changes (check the *Array Length Changes Week over Week* Table and check for large WoW changes for *raw\_uups\_\** features).   
5. Check for model performance ([example post](https://unity.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C06Q5D269DZ/p1757712224862729?thread_ts=1757710977.242679&channel=C06Q5D269DZ&message_ts=1757712224.862729))

Check the [Model Avg prediction Grafana dashboard](https://grafana.internal.unity3d.com/d/qMQ8n3rGk/cpi-valuation-metrics?orgId=1&from=now-7d&to=now&timezone=utc&var-ds=gS9XG4AVk&var-app=$__all&var-dsCloudMonitoring=000000146&var-branch=$__all&var-group=$__all&var-source=$__all&viewPanel=panel-3); [UV model grafana dashboard](https://grafana.internal.unity3d.com/goto/dfc9a16m7vp4wa?orgId=1); [New Max Bid Graphana](https://grafana.internal.unity3d.com/explore?schemaVersion=1&panes=%7B%221s9%22%3A%7B%22datasource%22%3A%22gS9XG4AVk%22%2C%22queries%22%3A%5B%7B%22refId%22%3A%22A%22%2C%22expr%22%3A%22histogram_quantile%280.99%2C+sum%28rate%28ads_valuation_composer_valuator_ecpm_distribution_bucket%5B5m%5D%29%29+by+%28le%29%29%22%2C%22range%22%3Atrue%2C%22instant%22%3Atrue%2C%22datasource%22%3A%7B%22type%22%3A%22prometheus%22%2C%22uid%22%3A%22gS9XG4AVk%22%7D%2C%22editorMode%22%3A%22code%22%2C%22legendFormat%22%3A%22__auto%22%7D%5D%2C%22range%22%3A%7B%22from%22%3A%22now-24h%22%2C%22to%22%3A%22now%22%7D%7D%7D&orgId=1)

# 4\. Incident Management Workflow   {#4.-incident-management-workflow}

1. **Alert Reception:** The on-call person will receive alerts via the designated monitoring system ([PagerDuty](https://unityops.pagerduty.com/schedules/PKG6QTK)).   
2. **Initial Triage:**  
   * Acknowledge the alert immediately.  
   * Assess the severity and impact of the incident.  
   * If the incident requires attention outside normal task prioritization, create an incident channel in slack (with the command \`/incident start\`)  
3. **Investigation:**  
   * Gather relevant information and logs to diagnose the issue.  
   * Utilize available tools and documentation for troubleshooting  
     * Example of investigation: [data contamination issue](#dataset-contamination-/-missing-data)  
     * Maintain the [list of relevant Dashboards](#appendix-1---list-of-relevant-dashboards) in the Appendix  
   * Collaborate with other team members if necessary.  
4. **Resolution:**  
   * Implement a solution or workaround to restore service.  
   * Test the fix to ensure the issue is resolved.  
5. **Documentation:**  
   * Record all steps taken, observations, and resolutions in the incident tracking system (incident channel).  
   * Update relevant documentation (e.g., [this SOP’s Appendix](#appendix-1---list-of-relevant-dashboards), [runbooks](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ads-audience-pinpointer/blob/2c2c8a6306dc2211c2beb3986d0a2472ae3fb746/runbooks), etc) if new insights are gained.  
   * Link the incident in [the tracker](#appendix-3---list-of-past-incidents), to keep tab on historical trends and see if some issues are recurring. (also useful: [BI's incident Looker dashboard](https://unitytech.looker.com/dashboards/3765?Priority=&Business+Unit=&Current+Status=&Event+Date=30+day+ago+for+30+day&Description=&Incident+Name=&tile_id42184.incidents_daily.business_unit=%22Unity-Ads%22))  
6. **Communication:**  
   * Inform stakeholders of the incident status and resolution.  
   * Ensure clear and concise communication throughout the incident lifecycle (using \`/incident update\` for better visibility).  
   * Follow up with a post-mortem analysis for critical incidents. See e.g. this [postmortem](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hZTcw7Ha7emZT6Nsn8OrIvocZ9zhthlWCcFqAvxtrY/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.mn2g1zwq0trs) as an example.

A similar process applies to the flow for production models failures. 

# 5\. Escalation Procedure

If an incident cannot be resolved by the primary on-call person within a reasonable timeframe (e.g., 30 minutes for critical issues), or if it requires specialized knowledge, the following escalation steps should be followed:

1. **Contact Team Lead:** Reach out to the team leads for assistance.  
   * [Jussi Kujala](mailto:jussikuj@unity3d.com)[Zenith Zeng](mailto:zenith.zeng@unity3d.com) [Chen Xue](mailto:chen.xue@unity3d.com) for science/business related topics  
   * Offline training @vector-offline-oncall   
   * Online serving @vector-online-oncall  
   * The **@ads-user-value-devs** slack handle can be used to quickly get visibility from all the UV team    
2. **Cross-Functional Teams:** For issues impacting other systems or teams, coordinate with the relevant external teams:   
   * MLOps: \#ads-audience-pinpointer-engineering  
   * dCPI service: \#ads-dd-dcpi-dev  
   * Data, upstream from the datagen: \#ads-app-data  
   * Experiment Platform: \#experimentation-platform  
   * Ads ML org: \#ads-ml-public 

# 6\. SOP of Tools and Resources \- To be filled by the team

The following tools and resources are essential for the on-call rotation:

* **Monitoring System:** [list of relevant Dashboards](#appendix-1---list-of-relevant-dashboards)  
* **Incident Tracking:** OpsBot ([\#sre-announce](https://unity.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C8ZHSNSAY))   
* Incident tracker by BI: [looker](https://unitytech.looker.com/dashboards/3765?Priority=&Business+Unit=&Current+Status=&Event+Date=30+day+ago+for+30+day&Description=&Incident+Name=)  
* **Documentation Portal:** This SOP, [main repo README](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ads-audience-pinpointer/blob/b231d142215308f859443af69c16d7b0353a4269/README.md), [runbooks](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ads-audience-pinpointer/blob/2c2c8a6306dc2211c2beb3986d0a2472ae3fb746/runbooks)  
  * [ML UASDK data issue SOP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1nSfKkcV89hulQIChaLAUU8fRTmj60e7WsoaYrbIf2ks/edit?usp=sharing)  
  * [ML MMP unattributed data issue SOP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Nhi4L-k8QuVgmQV-Hm5sJLv_i433Dmf1YPDFf8FotcI/edit?usp=sharing)  
* **Communication Channels:** Use the created incident channel, some wider communication can also be done in the internal team channel: [\#ads-ml-user-value-dev](https://unity.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C06Q5D269DZ)

7\. Post-Mortem Analysis  
For all critical incidents (P0), a post-mortem analysis will be conducted to identify the root cause, lessons learned, and preventative measures. The findings will be documented and shared with the team to improve future incident response, [example template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hZTcw7Ha7emZT6Nsn8OrIvocZ9zhthlWCcFqAvxtrY/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.mn2g1zwq0trs). Schedule post-mortem review meeting with the team and stakeholders. 

# Appendix 0 \- Investigation scenarios

## Dataset contamination / missing data {#dataset-contamination-/-missing-data}

This is inspired form [\#incident-2025-08-19-3](https://unity.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C09AZKJU077)

Process: 

1. Create the incident channel (\`/incident start\`). See the [Incident Channel Tooling](#appendix-4---incident-channel-tooling) section for more details on incident channel and their management.   
2. Summarize the discussions that happened before the creation of the channel ([example](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C09AZKJU077/p1755609832005339))  
3. Check for model misbehavior  
   1. Find the exact time of the problematic model deployment using the [Triton panel](https://grafana.internal.unity3d.com/d/WFpzgk6Vk/triton?orgId=1&var-ds=gS9XG4AVk&var-service=All&from=now-7d&to=now&viewPanel=2) ([example](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C09AZKJU077/p1755615701144999))  
   2. Check for abnormal changes of mean dCPI, zero valuations or other online metrics from the [dCPI valuation metrics Grafana](https://grafana.internal.unity3d.com/d/qMQ8n3rGk/cpi-valuation-metrics?orgId=1&refresh=30s&var-service=mz-dd-dynamic-cpi&var-ds=unity-ads-cpi-direct-prd%2Fmetrics&var-cacheFilling=mz-dd-dynamic-cpi-cachefilling&var-loadtest=mz-dd-dynamic-cpi-loadtest&var-trafficGen=mz-dd-dynamic-cpi-traffic-generator&var-app=All&var-dsCloudMonitoring=unity-ads-cpi-direct-prd%2Fgcp&var-branch=All&var-group=All&var-source=All&from=now-14d&to=now) ([example](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C09AZKJU077/p1755614326026289?thread_ts=1755613267.101449&cid=C09AZKJU077))  
   3. Changes of valuation metrics over ad requests (i.e. in the above panel) doesn’t always translate to meaningful changes of the delivery metrics (over impressions or installs). If the incident started \>2h ago, check either of the [Direct Demand Implys](#imply-cubes) to confirm business impact level. ([example](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C09AZKJU077/p1755613588536589?thread_ts=1755611537.428289&cid=C09AZKJU077))  
4. If model behavior has negative business impact and a temporary fix is required, revert to the last known working model. See the [model rollback process section](#model-rollback-processes).   
5. If the data is missing due to a failed datagen run, the next automated run will automatically fix the issue. If data contamination is the issue, it might be relevant to blacklist the faulty advertiser (see [the blacklist readme](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ads-audience-pinpointer/blob/2c2c8a6306dc2211c2beb3986d0a2472ae3fb746/runbooks/BLACKLIST.md)), then the daily training run will automatically be fixed. If required, start a manual run for quicker model recovery.    
6. Confirm that the problematic behavior identified in 3\. are revolved after the next model deployment  
7. Return to step 5\. of the [Incident Management Workflow](#4.-incident-management-workflow)

Initial list from \#incident-2025-01-30-1 [postmortem](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hZTcw7Ha7emZT6Nsn8OrIvocZ9zhthlWCcFqAvxtrY/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.mn2g1zwq0trs). Please maintain this list moving forward. 

## Imply cubes {#imply-cubes}

For most incidents related to revenue drop, Imply will be the first tool used in the investigation. It is useful for slicing and dicing until a correlation between the drop and a product / platform / MMP / etc is identified. Most useful Imply cubes: 

- [Supply Demand Internal](https://internal-v2-1.pivot.int-prd-imply.unity3d.com/pivot/i/babc2f7b94abb83c1e/uAds_Demand_Supply_Internal_\(billing_&_finance\)) (does contain post-install outcomes but less features and time granularity)   
- [Direct Demand(event\_ts)](https://internal-v2-1.pivot.int-prd-imply.unity3d.com/pivot/i/e2ddc3d81dc11ed11b/uAds_Direct_Demand_ML_\(event_ts_timestamp\)) (for revenue analysis)  
- [Direct Demand(ad\_request\_ts)](https://internal-v2-1.pivot.int-prd-imply.unity3d.com/pivot/i/576b99984fbe9f2728/uAds_Direct_Demand_Post_Install_ML_\(ad_request_timestamp\)) (for a/b test analysis)

See [this post](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C04R4CKP2B1/p1758546188110279) for the latest specifications of the first 2 Implys (as of 2025-09-22)

All products [imply](https://internal-v2-1.pivot.int-prd-imply.unity3d.com/pivot/home)

## Bigquery

* [Post-install online colab to comparate EP experiments](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ads-mega-model/wiki/User-Value:-online-experiment-BQ-analysis-script)  
* [online stability colab to plot model version predictions over time](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/19EvzmHDXnJSbbbKlwmVkmHOjYIfi8cQ7?usp=sharing): useful to diagnose instability  
* [dCPI valuation colab](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1ve2Q2r92EKLLR-egwliM_GhuM2ScXU04?usp=sharing) to analyze valuation changes over time, before campaign selection. For example, discount factor, audience count etc.  
* Sample query to check the features in the training data

	

```sql
select date, 
avg(if(post_install_adrev_sum_d7 > 0, 1, 0)) as avg_posi_adrev_d7_rate,
avg(if(post_install_adrev_sum_d7 < 0, 1, 0)) as avg_neg_adrev_d7_rate,
avg(if(post_install_deposit_sum_d7 > 0, 1, 0)) as pos_dep_d7_rate,
AVG(CASE WHEN post_install_deposit_sum_d7 > 0 THEN post_install_deposit_sum_d7 END) AS avg_pos_dep_d7,
1.0 * safe_divide(countif(post_install_deposit_sum_d1 > 0), countif(post_install_deposit_sum_d1 >= 0)) AS valid_deposit_rate_d1
FROM `unity-ads-dd-ds-prd.user_value_incremental_datagen.unified_user_value_v3`
where date >= '2025-07-01'
and platform = 'ios'
and source = 'mmp_attributed'
group by date
```

# Appendix 2 \- model recovery processes

## Model rollback processes {#model-rollback-processes}

1. [Rollback process for UL common inference](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TlYRfXw-YHvlls16AAgQCbbIBeXH2NM8VviieKtYPhU/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.9z93ecfu8qik)  
2. [Pause model updates for UL common inference](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C06Q5D269DZ/p1765914096672439)  
3. [Rollback process for UL (without model name change for AB test)](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C09AZKJU077/p1755616498122999),   
   1. If the rollback lasts more than the retraining frequency of the production model, you’ll also need to disable the workflow  
   2. After the recovery,   
      1. Examine the impacted data, exclude problematic data if need, train the model  
      2. re-enable the workflow  
   3. How to find the workflow?  
      1. All workflows are listed here: [https://console.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/pipelines/schedules?project=unity-applied-research-ml-test](https://console.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/pipelines/schedules?project=unity-applied-research-ml-test)   
      2. One can search key words \`user-value\` and select the correct version. For example, v3-40![][image1]  
      3. Click to go into the workflow page, click on Pause.  
4. [Rollback process for MegaModel (with model name change for AB testing)](https://unity.slack.com/archives/C06Q5D269DZ/p1756228701286389?thread_ts=1756224898.388819&cid=C06Q5D269DZ). 

## Model re-training & data re-generation / backfilling process

1. For UV MegaModel:   
   1. Clone the latest production KF UV datagen run (see [this KF experiment](https://kubeflow-platform.iap.mlp.unity3d.com/_/pipeline/?ns=kubeflow-audience-pinpointer#/experiments/details/5a34e18d-ac6c-49b3-b3c1-0942d4c45a09))  
   2. Clone the latest Vertex MegaModel training run (see [these Vertex Pipelines Schedules](https://console.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/pipelines/schedules?project=unity-applied-research-ml-test), filter for ‘main-runner-depositor’ and select the latest. There should be only one active)  
2. For UV UL:   
   1. Backfill the UV incremental raw datagen  
      (If there are upstream IPJ changes, skip this if not)  
   2. Backfill preprocessed data in UL  
      (when there are significant changes in feature mapping, consider backfilling for update\_mappings as well. If the difference is small we may skip it, as this runs serially and can run for a long time)  
   3. Combine training data and train the UV UL model

## Preprocess Data Backfill Process (high level)

1. Identify the workflow of Preprocessing  
2. Change the target\_dates accordingly, this can be done by either:  
   1. Hard code target\_dates to list of dates (e.g. \["2026-01-01", "2026-01-02"\])  
   2. Update DAY\_OFFSETS (e.g. DAY\_OFFSETS \= list(range(100)), if we want to backfill the last 100 days, counting back from the latest available install date)  
3. Comment out workflow decorations: @schedule and @slack\_alert (to prevent spamming)  
4. Comment out other workflow steps:  
   1. Not needed for data backfill:  
      1. check\_raw\_data  
      2. model\_train and steps after train  
   2. Might need to keep:  
      1. update\_mappings: may be needed when there are significant change to categorical features  
      2. combine\_training\_data: may be useful when evaluation is using combined data, but need to tune train\_end\_date as needed  
5. Comment out the retry of datagen (specially for backfills of many days, to prevent repeatedly restarting the whole step when only few days failed)

Notes for base workflow:

* day\_offsets is configurable as part of UserValueWorkflowConfig  
  * Remember to update datagen\_task\_parallelism for large backfills  
* Commenting out other workflow steps can be done by adding @skip\_step decoration to the unwanted steps (the list of all steps in base workflow can be found in [readme](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/vector-ai-unity-learner/tree/main/src/unity_learner/experiment_repo/unified_user_value#workflow-steps))  
  * If only 1 of the step is needed, can also directly use UserValueWorkflowStepLogic to build the step (similar to [e2e test](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/vector-ai-unity-learner/blob/0022aabce90a423d51ed3f45cb1c45d02a5d409a/src/unity_learner/experiment_repo/unified_user_value/v1_e2e_test_workflow/workflow.py#L148))

## Blacklist some dates’ data

### game level block

To block certain target\_game\_id (mask the corresponding labels in training data to \-1) over some range of dates, follow this to add records in the blocklist table: [link](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/ads-event-blocklist/blob/master/usage.md)

### date level block

To blacklist some dates (completely exclude the date from training data), add it to blacklisted\_dates\_v2, this will block the dates from all user value experiments:  
Use platform \= “unified” and model\_type \= “user\_value”, and run the python script locally, example:

```py
from unity_learner.db_manager.data_pipeline_status_manager import DataPipelineStatusManager

dm = DataPipelineStatusManager()
dm.blacklist_dates(platform="unified", model_type="user_value", dates=["2026-05-27"], blacklist_reason="#incident-2026-05-27-1")
```

# Appendix 4 \- Incident channel tooling {#appendix-4---incident-channel-tooling}

To create and manage an incident channel: 

1. Start by typing \`/incident start\` in any slack channel![][image2]  
   1. Fill out the incident description  
      ![][image3]  
      ![][image4]  
   2. For visible revenue drops, use SEV0 & P0.  
       If the concern is model performance, but the impact is not yet visible in business metrics, go for SEV1 & P1.   
      If it’s an issue with e.g. training pipelines failing intermittently, which compromise the ability of the team to work but doesn’t impact system performance, go for SEV2 / P2.   
2. Once created, invite all the relevant stakeholders to the channel  
3. Re-post the relevant post/threads to give context to the people joining the channel  
4. As the incident investigation / mitigation progresses, provide regular updates through the \`\\incident update\` dialog box.   
   1. This is better than posting in the channel since it’s also communicated more broadly (e.g. [\#sre-announce](https://unity.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C8ZHSNSAY)) and provide a high level view of the incident to external stakeholders.   
5. Once the issue is resolved with a proper fix (not just mitigated), use \`\\incident resolve\`  
6. Prepare a post-mortem doc (example [postmortem](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14hZTcw7Ha7emZT6Nsn8OrIvocZ9zhthlWCcFqAvxtrY/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.mn2g1zwq0trs))  
7. Schedule a meeting with the main stakeholders of the incident  
   1. Discuss in particular the follow up tasks to reduce the chances of re-occurrence  
8. Once the follow-up tasks tracked in the post-mortem are completed, close the incident with \`\\incident close\`
